corrections.why: The 1952 survey description gives a 14-foot square building about 25 feet high; 4.3 m (about 14 ft) matches only the cab width, not the height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Former Fire Lookout Sites register says completed 1937; West Lookouts says completed 1939 by the Seiad CCC camp. A December 1928 newspaper item also describes an observer at a China Mountain lookout. The story gives the register date and the West Lookouts date and does not choose between them.
The register describes a 20 enclosed timber tower without units; the 1952 survey description gives about 25 feet high for the building. The record uses 7.6 m (25 ft) from the survey description.
The brief notes OpenStreetMap shows the lookout as standing. The OpenStreetMap page gives a name and tag but no date or condition, so it is not treated as evidence that the structure stands.

sources.title: China Creek (China Peak entry), Forest Lookouts

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 4.3 appears to be the 14-foot cab width; the 1952 survey description gives about 25 ft for the building, so 7.6 m is proposed. The register's '20 enclosed timber tower' has no unit, so it is not used for height. Built year conflicts (1937 register vs 1939 West Lookouts; a 1928 observer item may refer to an earlier structure), and both dates are reported. The OpenStreetMap entry has no date and does not show a standing structure; the brief's osm=standing is not supported by the page read. Staffing is the last documented period in the sources (1963). Nothing read describes the site today. The 1972 structure's parts reportedly went to a nearby cabin, which is not a source for the site itself. The West Lookouts page is a hobbyist compilation that quotes newspapers and the NGS survey text; quotes were taken from its own text.
